N/A -- no panic, this is a data-corruption/console-visibility bug, not a crash.

Applying an unrelated field change (e.g. `use_in_dr_mode`) to an existing zpa_application_segment should not alter that segment's AppProtection or Active Directory Inspection configuration, regardless of whether those were enabled directly in the console. The segment should remain visible/findable in the console's main Application Segments list.

If AppProtection (or Active Directory Inspection) was enabled on the segment via the console, applying *any* unrelated Terraform update to that segment corrupts the linked Inspection configuration and the segment disappears from the console's main Application Segments list (though it remains functional and still reachable via its Segment Group's member list -- see "Important Factoids").

Specifically for AppProtection: the segment-level "Auto App Protection: Enabled" toggle reverts, and the per-domain config becomes: AppProtection checkbox checked, Port = 443, no protocol selected, "Use Untrusted Certificates" checked -- an incomplete configuration (selecting a protocol then prompts for a certificate before the segment can be saved). Manually unchecking AppProtection for that domain immediately restores the segment's visibility in the main list.

blocks.text: reachable via its Segment Group). "Auto App Protection" has reverted to a per-domain checkbox, checked, Port 443, no protocol selected, "Use Untrusted Certificates" checked.

Reproduced twice independently on two different segments (one pre-existing production segment, one created fresh for testing), with the control case (step

We also tested with Active Directory Inspection (Kerberos/LDAP/SMB) enabled instead of AppProtection: the same kind of unrelated update reverted AD Inspection to disabled and re-typed the per-domain companion object as an AppProtection configuration instead (not an AD Inspection one) -- Port = ANY, no protocol, no certificate. The segment did NOT go invisible in this instance, unlike the AppProtection case (Port 443, no protocol). We suspect the underlying disturbance to the linked Inspection object happens either way, but whether the resulting state actually breaks console visibility depends on whether that state is invalid by the API's own internal rules.

blocks.item: The segment is not actually broken while "invisible" -- it continues to

blocks.text: function normally (policy evaluation, connector routing), confirmed via browser devtools showing the API still returns its full data. It's a console list/search rendering issue, not a data-integrity failure.

blocks.item: It's still findable via its Segment Group's member list, and can be repaired

blocks.text: from there.
destroy+recreate) also restores visibility.

blocks.item: The zpa_application_segment resource's documented schema has zero attributes

blocks.text: related to AppProtection/Inspection, so nothing in our Terraform config sets or clears this -- the update itself appears to disturb an existing linked Inspection object the base resource has no knowledge of.

blocks.item: The documented zpa_application_segment_inspection schema has no attribute

blocks.text: equivalent to the console's "Use Untrusted Certificates" option -- certificate_id is the only documented option when application_protocol=HTTPS, with no alternative for untrusted/self-signed certs. This means we currently can't even test whether managing AppProtection via zpa_application_segment_inspection in Terraform (alongside the base segment) would prevent this, since we can't declare the exact working configuration.

blocks.item: #500 (fix: Fixed ZPA Specialized Application Segments Update Functions) --

blocks.text: same category of bug (update payloads not properly preserving a linked companion object's identity), but for the specialized resources' own updates. Our case is the base zpa_application_segment's update corrupting a linked Inspection object it has no schema knowledge of at all -- the same problem, one level removed.
@(user) Upgrade to the latest version [v4.4.12.](https://github.com/zscaler/terraform-provider-zpa/releases/tag/v4.4.12)

We would like to emphasize that AppProtection (Auto App Protection) and Active Directory Inspection are not supported attributes of the zpa_application_segment resource. They are supported only by the zpa_application_segment_inspection resource, which is the resource to use for any application segment with AppProtection or AD Inspection enabled. Please refer to the documentation: https://registry.terraform.io/providers/zscaler/zpa/latest/docs/resources/zpa_application_segment_inspection
The "Use Untrusted Certificates" option you mentioned is available there as common_apps_dto.apps_config.trust_untrusted_cert.

To resolve the customer case, move the affected segment to zpa_application_segment_inspection (import it into that resource and remove it from zpa_application_segment) and manage it there going forward.
